sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.53,50,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by her in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 25.08.2019 when the petitioner was going towards Jalahalli corss from Gangamma Gudi Circle in front of Cluny Convent, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-M-680 was driving in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner's Scooty from behind.
Due to which, the petitioner fell down along with her vehicle and sustained (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.2427/2021 injuries to her right leg, left leg.

Immediately after the accident,
petitioner was shifted by the driver of the offending vehicle to Sun Orthopaedic Hospital and after first aid she was taken to Sparsha Hospital on 26.08.2019 and then she was admitted to Vijaya Nagara Hospital on 11.09.2019 and on the same day she underwent surgery.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 25 years and she was working women.

On receipt of complaint, the Jalahalli traffic police have registered a case in their crime No.0086/2019 on 18.09.2019 against the driver of Car bearing reg.No.KA- 50-M-680 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC.
Petitioner further contended, she has spent Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical, transportation and other miscellaneous expenses.

The first respondent being the insurer and the second respondent being the owner of the Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-M-680 are jointly and severally (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.2427/2021 liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner constrained to file a petition.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal and filed their respective written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, wherein respondent denies all the allegations made in the petition and also the issuance of an Insurance policy in respect of the Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-M-680 is to be verify.

Further contended that, driver of the vehicle has not valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of petition averments in toto and also denied the manner of accident.
With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition.
The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that,
wherein
respondent denies all the allegations made in the petition

. Respondent also denied the age,
income of the petitioner.
Further respondent contended that, the said accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
Further denied the medical expenses occurred to the treatment taken by the petitioner.

Further contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly Noothana A.S vs New India Assurance Co Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117831493/
2 excessive, exorbitant, fanciful.

sentences.text: Further respondent admitted that Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50- M-680 was insured with the respondent No.1.
Further contended that, petitioner has lodged the complaint after lapse of 24 days of the alleged accident.
Further contended that, driver of the vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.2427/2021 has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 25.08.2019 at about 12.15 pm., when the petitioner was riding Yamaha Scooty bearing reg.No.KA-04-JT-3348 towards Jalahalli Cross from Gangamma Gudi Circle, infront of Cluny Convent, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing Reg.No.KA-50-M-680 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner motor cycle.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injury as alleged in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum ?

From whom ?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove her case, the petitioner herself examined as PW.1.
Dr. Shekar.M has examined as PW.2 and in all got marked Ex.P.1 to 25.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 has not led its side evidence.

6. Heard arguments and perused the materials (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.2427/2021 available on record.
7.

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
-:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:-

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 25.08.2019 when she was going towards Jalahalli corss from Gangamma Gudi Circle in front of Cluny Convent, at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-M-680 was driving in a rash and negligent manner and hit to her Scooty from behind.
Due to which, she fell down along with her vehicle and sustained injuries to her right leg, left leg.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, petitioner herself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief- examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.

She has also got marked complaint, FIR, (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.2427/2021 panchanama, rough sketch, notice, reply to notice,
IMV reports, charge sheet, medical bills and prescriptions, discharge summaries, Aadhar card and PAN card etc., at Ex.P1 to P25.
10.
I have perused Ex-P1 to Ex-P9.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 25.08.2019 at around 12.15 pm., and the FIR in crime No.0086/2019 came to be registered on 18.09.2019 at 15.00 at Jalahalli traffic Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
Further
the records reveal that, petitioner herself has lodged the complaint marked at Ex.P.1.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In her cross-examination she has specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.1 that, due to the rash and negligent riding by her, the alleged accident got occurred.
(SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.2427/2021 PW.1 denied the same.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve her version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet - Ex.P.9 filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of Maruthi Ritz Vxi Car bearing reg.No.KA-50-M-680 which belongs to the respondent No.2 and respondent No.1 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

11. Issue No.2: In view of answering Issue No.1 in (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.2427/2021 the affirmative,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries, pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges,
conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
let me discuss one by one:

a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering: PW.1 has contended that due to the accident she sustained fracture of left leg and doctors at Vijaya Nagara Hospital opined as right knee ACL avulsion fracture, arthroscopic right knee ACL fracture, Fixation SA pm 11.09.2019 pain and swelling over the right knee, fracture in lateral tibial plateau and head of fibula, moderate to sever lipohemarthrosis with periarticular soft tissue edema in popliteal fossa and also opined said injuries are grievous in nature.
PW.1 also contended that, orthoscopic right (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.2427/2021 knee, ALC was done.
In order to prove injuries caused to her, PW.1 has not produced wound certificate but on perusal of other medical records it seems to be genuine.

sentences.text: The record shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and she has examined Dr.Shekar.M as PW.2 and he has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
Therefore, by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.

Pw.1 contended that immediately after the accident she was shifted to Sun Orthopedic Hospital,
Bengaluru after first aid she was shifted to Sparsha Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Again she got admitted to Vijaya Nagara Hospital for treatment.
PW.1 has produced (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.2427/2021 medical bills marked at Ex.P.10 to a tune of Rs.2,50,600/- along with 7 medical prescriptions.

On perusal of the Ex.P.10 - medical bills,
it came to know that, after sum up it amounts to Rs.2,05,600/- and those bills are genuine.

Hence,
in all the Tribunal is of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,05,600/- is just and reasonable towards Medical expenses.
c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges: Petitioner has produced 3 discharge summaries of Vijayanagar Hospital marked at Ex.P.12, 13 and 20.
On perusal of the same, it came to know that, Ex.P.13 and Ex.P.20 are one and the same.

As per Ex.P.12 and 13,
Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 11.09.2019 to 13.09.2019 and from 12.10.2020 to 14.10.2020 in total for a period of 6 days and during the time of treatment the petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.2427/2021 of Rs.1,000/- per day for 6 days and by including towards conveyance, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:
PW.1 has contended that she was working at Private Bank as Assistant and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, petitioner has not produced any document.
Therefore, in the absence of positive documents regarding her income, this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2019 at 14,000/- p.m.,
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2019 treated as Rs.14,000/- p.m.

Considering the age,
nature of injuries, treatment given & duration of her stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out her avocation normally for at least 2 to 3 months.

Thus, by taking into account the notional income (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.2427/2021 of PW.1, this Tribunal awards Rs.42,000/- (14,000/- X 3)
towards loss of income during treatment period.

e) Towards Loss of Income due to Disability: PW.1 has examined Dr.Shekar.M,
Orthopaedic surgeon and Assistant Professor Orthopedics, Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopedics, Bengaluru as PW.2 and through him got marked OPD sheet, X-ray and disability assessment form marked at Ex.P.17 to 19.

sentences.text:
PW.2 has contended that, patient was diagnosed to have abrasion over the right knee, right ankle and right foot, had pain and swelling over right knee, MRI right knee showed SCL avulsion fracture,
fracture head of fibula and she underwent artroscopic right knee ACL avulsion fracture fixation with screw on 11.09.2019 and discharged on 13.09.2019.

Further contended that, patient further admitted on 12.10.2020 at Sparsh Hospital and underwent orthroscopic implant removal and lateral meniscus anterior horn balancing right knee on (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.2427/2021 13.10.2020 and discharged on 14.10.2020.
Patient came to their hospital on 08.04.2025 for assessment of disability.
PW.2 assessed permanent physical disability of right lower limb of 42.05% and to the whole body of 14.01%.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.2 has assessed whole body disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 11% whole body disability which cannot be ruled out.
During cross examination PW.2 has deposed that, he has not treated the petitioner and implants are removed and admitted that, after 4 years he has assessed disability.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.15 - Aadhar card in order to prove her age.
As per said document, she was born on 05.02.1994 and as on date of accident she was aged about 25 years.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered as 25 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "18" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.2427/2021 case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
14,000 x 12 x 18 x 11% = Rs.3,32,640/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.3,32,640/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities:

Petitioner has contended that, due to accidental injuries she cannot able to walk for a long and stand more than 10 minutes, not able to squat on floor and not able to use Indian toilet, she is inability to earn and become permanent disabled.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) Towards future medical expenses: PW.2 has not suggested to the petitioner for any future medication.
Therefore, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.2427/2021 any interest.

12. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

 a. Towards injury pain and .50,000/-
 suffering  b. Towards medical expenses .2,05,600/-

Total compensation .6,90,240/-
13.
Regarding Liability:

It is the contention of the respondent that, after lapse of 24 days after occurrence of alleged accident, the complaint has been lodged by the petitioner and it clearly goes to prove the collusion between (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.2427/2021 the petitioner and the owner of the Car bearing No.KA-50- M-680.
Mere dispute, respondent has not taken any steps with regard to it.
Respondent has failed to disprove the negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-50-M- 680.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.1 being the Insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay compensation of .6,90,240/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

(SCCH-9) 19 MVC.No.2427/2021  The petitioner is entitled for total  compensation amount of .6,90,240/-
(Rupees six lakhs ninety thousand two hundred forty only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on Noothana A.S vs New India Assurance Co Ltd on 3 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117831493/
